en: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, and Waki' informed us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh and Yahya ibn Habib both narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; all of them from Isma'il with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: We entered upon Khabbab while he had been cauterized seven times on his belly, and he said: "Were it not that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade us from praying for death, I would have prayed for it."

Hamid ibn 'Umar narrated to me: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us: 'Asim narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, while Anas was alive on that day; Anas said: "Were it not that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'None of you should wish for death,' I would have wished for it."

Ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Salamah—narrated to us; both from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that he said: "due to harm that has afflicted him."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should wish for death due to harm that has befallen him; but if he must wish, let him say: 'O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and take my soul when death is good for me.'"

Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us: Al-Harith—and he is Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhubab—narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Mina', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should say: 'O Allah, forgive me if You will; O Allah, have mercy on me if You will.' Let him be resolute in supplication, for indeed Allah does whatever He wills, and there is no compeller for Him."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you supplicates, he should not say: 'O Allah, forgive me if You will'; rather, let him be resolute in asking, and let him magnify his desire, for indeed nothing is too grand for Allah that He gives."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to us from Ibn 'Ulayyah; Abu Bakr said: Isma'il Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you supplicates, let him be resolute in supplication, and let him not say: 'O Allah, if You will, grant me,' for indeed there is no compeller of Allah."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah; and from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names—one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise." And Hammam added from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Indeed, He is Witr (Odd/One) and loves the witr."

'Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi 'Umar all narrated to us from Sufyan—and the wording is 'Amr's: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "To Allah belong ninety-nine names; whoever memorizes them will enter Paradise. And indeed, Allah is Witr and loves the witr." And in the narration of Ibn Abi 'Umar: "whoever enumerates them."

Umayyah ibn Bistam al-'Ayshi narrated to us: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us: Rawh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was traveling along the road to Mecca and passed by a mountain called Jumdan, and he said: "Travel on, this is Jumdan; the mufarridun have gone ahead." They asked: "And who are the mufarridun, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The men who remember Allah abundantly and the women who remember [Him]."

And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with its meaning.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab al-Qa'nabi narrated to me: Al-Mughirah—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of one of you than one of you is with his lost animal when he finds it."

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him wherever he remembers Me. By Allah, Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you finding his lost animal in the desert. And whoever draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; and whoever draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and when he comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—both narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than them. And if he approaches near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; and if he approaches near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qaysi narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father with this chain of transmission, and he did not mention: "when he comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar ibn 'Uthman al-'Abdi narrated to us: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—and Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sulayman—and he is al-Taymi—from Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'When My servant draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; and when he draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and when he comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed.'"

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.'"

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—so he mentioned several hadiths among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah said: 'When My servant meets Me by a handspan, I meet him by an arm's length; and when he meets Me by an arm's length, I meet him by a fathom; and when he meets Me by a fathom, I come to him faster.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash with this chain of transmission, and he did not mention: "and if he draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Zuhayr ibn Harb—and the wording is Qutaybah's—both narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than them. And if he draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; and if he draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed.'"

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward similar to the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their rewards; and whoever calls to misguidance will bear a burden of sin similar to the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their sins."

Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Abu Shurayh narrated to me that Abu al-Aswad narrated to him, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "O son of my sister, it has reached me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr passes by us going for Hajj, so meet him and ask him, for he has acquired abundant knowledge from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." He said: So I met him and asked him about things that he mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). 'Urwah said: Among what he mentioned was that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah does not strip away knowledge from people by snatching it away; rather, He takes away the scholars, so knowledge is taken away with them, and there remain among the people ignorant leaders who give them religious verdicts without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray." 'Urwah said: When I narrated that to 'A'ishah, she considered it momentous and questioned it, saying: "Did he narrate to you that he heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say this?" 'Urwah said: Until when the following year arrived, she said to him: "'Abdullah ibn 'Amr has arrived, so meet him and open conversation with him until you ask him about the hadith that he mentioned to you regarding knowledge." He said: So I met him and asked him, and he mentioned it to me similar to what he had narrated to me the first time. 'Urwah said: When I informed her of that, she said: "I think nothing except that he has spoken the truth; I see that he neither added anything to it nor took anything away."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Humran narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far: My father Ja'far informed me, from 'Umar ibn al-Hakam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of Hisham ibn 'Urwah.

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad and Abu Mu'awiyah informed us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Idris, Abu Usamah, Ibn Numayr, and 'Abdah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Ali narrated to us; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj informed us; all of them from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of Jarir; and he added in the hadith of 'Umar ibn 'Ali: "Then I met 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr at the turn of the year and asked him, and he recounted the hadith to us just as he had narrated it, saying: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying...'"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, Allah does not seize knowledge by snatching it away from people, but He seizes knowledge by taking away the scholars, until when He leaves no scholar, people take ignorant leaders who, when asked, deliver religious verdicts without knowledge, thus going astray and leading others astray."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, who said: I was sitting with 'Abdullah and Abu Musa while they were conversing, and Abu Musa said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, Ibn Numayr, and Ishaq al-Hanzali all narrated to us from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr ibn Abi al-Nadr narrated to us: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said; (H) and al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya narrated to me: Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Sulayman, from Shaqiq, who said: I was sitting with 'Abdullah and Abu Musa while they were conversing, and they both said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... similar to the hadith of Waki' and Ibn Numayr.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Waki' and my father both narrated to us, saying: Al-A'mash narrated to us; (H) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj—and the wording is his—narrated to me: Waki' narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, who said: I was sitting with 'Abdullah and Abu Musa, and they both said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, ahead of the Hour there will be days in which knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will descend, and al-harj will become rampant; and al-harj is killing."
